title: Clarifying words that no longer fit
meaning: Careful clarification helps you name a changed meaning clearly, even while an earlier understanding of a promise still needs an emotional farewell.
text: Familiar words can remain longer than the meaning once placed in them. The Emperor in the physical position of Vishuddha helps ask a question without hidden assumptions and state terms directly. The Moon in energy supports attentive clarification: hearing what is meant now in place of guessing. Death in emotions describes the ending of an earlier version. Even a calm reply can bring regret when loved wording no longer expresses a current wish. An honest exchange about this change leaves both people free from needing immediate pleasure in the new meaning.

Suppose you clarify the familiar “We’ll talk about everything tonight”. It now means a brief exchange of news rather than the long conversation that once ended the day. **A clarified meaning allows an earlier expectation a farewell.** You can name what mattered about the older exchange and discuss a realistic chance to return to it sometimes. Familiar words are freed from silently carrying a promise nobody accepted again.

The difficulty arises if a feeling of loss makes every new sentence seem to conceal another ending. Exploring meaning remains useful, while emotion can enlarge it into endless checking for change. A concrete answer about this evening allows the actual difference to be discussed without making it explain everything supposedly disappearing from your communication.
